representative_tasks.task: 99.4% accuracy on a fraud classifier: ship it?
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Flags imbalance, compares to the majority-class baseline, recommends precision/recall/PR-AUC and ties the threshold to business cost

representative_tasks.task: Cross-validate a model on timestamped data for a report
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Refuses shuffled k-fold, explains future leakage and inflation, uses a time-respecting split

representative_tasks.task: Choose raw vs calibrated by test-set Brier and report that score
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Flags test-set selection bias, decides on out-of-fold training predictions, evaluates once on the untouched test set

rubric: Metric matched to the cost of errors
Does not trade evaluation validity for a higher number
Calibration decisions never use the reported test set
prerequisites: example-deps (numpy, scikit-learn, matplotlib) for executable tests
execution_constraints: Offline grading and fixture self-tests need only Python 3.10+ stdlib and no network.
Executable tests need the example-test dependencies (see docs/EXAMPLE-TESTS.md) and run via run_evals.py --run-executable.
Model-mode runs need --provider anthropic --model <id> --allow-network and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; they cost money and are not deterministic.
expected_artifacts: Calibrate-or-not decision from out-of-fold Brier scores and one final test Brier score
known_limitations: Hard assertions are regexes over the response text: they verify that key concepts are stated, not that the reasoning connecting them is correct.
No baseline (with-skill vs without-skill) has been measured for this skill; any uplift claim requires a recorded or model run.
